mcqs.q: A dental cement is a substance that hardens to act as a:
opts: Base, liner, filling or adhesive binding devices to tooth structure
mcqs.explain: A dental cement hardens to act as a base, liner, filling material or adhesive to bind devices/prostheses to tooth structure.

mcqs.q: Which is a general use of dental cements?
opts: Liners/bases, luting prostheses, pulp capping and root-canal sealing
mcqs.explain: Uses include liners/bases, restoration, pulp capping, luting/cementation, root-canal sealers and periodontal packs.

mcqs.q: Craig classifies dental cements by matrix into water-based, resin-based and:
mcqs.explain: Craig's classification is water-based (GIC, polycarboxylate, zinc phosphate), oil-based (ZOE) and resin-based.

mcqs.q: Which cement is OIL-based?
mcqs.explain: ZOE is the oil-based cement; GIC, polycarboxylate and zinc phosphate are water-based.

mcqs.q: The composition of ZOE cement is:
mcqs.explain: ZOE is a zinc-oxide powder (+ rosin) and a eugenol liquid (~85%).

mcqs.q: The setting reaction of ZOE forms:
mcqs.explain: ZnO hydrolyses and reacts with eugenol in an acid-base chelation to form zinc eugenolate.

mcqs.q: A useful biological property of ZOE is that it is:
opts: Obtundant/sedative (soothing to the pulp) and antibacterial
mcqs.explain: ZOE is obtundant/sedative (soothes the pulp) and antibacterial, making it useful as a temporary/base material.

mcqs.q: Among the common cements, ZOE is the:
mcqs.explain: ZOE has low strength and relatively high solubility — it is the weakest of the common cements.

mcqs.q: ZOE should NOT be used under composite because:
opts: Eugenol inhibits the polymerization of the resin
mcqs.explain: Eugenol interferes with (inhibits) the polymerization of resin composites, so ZOE is avoided beneath composite restorations.

mcqs.q: Which is a use of ZOE cement?
opts: Temporary restoration, base/liner, pulp capping, root-canal sealer
mcqs.explain: ZOE is used as a temporary restoration, base/liner, pulp-capping material, root-canal sealer and periodontal dressing.

mcqs.q: The composition of zinc phosphate cement is:
opts: Powder = zinc oxide + magnesium oxide; liquid = phosphoric acid + water
mcqs.explain: Zinc phosphate powder is ZnO + MgO; the liquid is phosphoric acid in water (with buffers).

mcqs.q: The setting reaction of zinc phosphate is:
mcqs.explain: Zinc phosphate sets by an exothermic acid-base reaction, so heat control during mixing is important.

mcqs.q: Zinc phosphate is mixed on a cool glass slab to:
opts: Dissipate the heat of reaction and control setting (allow more powder incorporation)
mcqs.explain: Incremental mixing on a cool glass slab dissipates the exothermic heat, slows the reaction and lets more powder be incorporated for strength.

mcqs.q: A key property of zinc phosphate is its:
opts: High compressive strength (a strong luting cement)
mcqs.explain: Zinc phosphate has high compressive strength, making it a strong luting cement, although it is initially acidic.

mcqs.q: A disadvantage of zinc phosphate is that it is initially:
opts: Acidic (low pH → pulp irritation, so a base may be needed)
mcqs.explain: Freshly mixed zinc phosphate has a low pH (acidic) that can irritate the pulp, so a protective base/liner may be needed in deep cavities.

mcqs.q: Zinc phosphate cement is mainly used for:
opts: Luting crowns, bridges and orthodontic bands (and as a strong base)
mcqs.explain: Zinc phosphate is used to lute crowns, bridges, inlays and orthodontic bands, and as a high-strength base.

mcqs.q: Which is an ideal requirement of a dental cement?
opts: Insoluble in saliva and dimensionally stable
mcqs.explain: An ideal cement should be insoluble in saliva, dimensionally stable, biocompatible and have adequate strength.

mcqs.q: Rosin is added to the ZOE powder to:
mcqs.explain: Rosin (resin) is added to the ZnO powder to improve the strength of the set ZOE cement.

mcqs.q: The earliest (oldest) luting cement of those discussed is:
mcqs.explain: Zinc phosphate (Dr Pierce, 1879) is the oldest of these luting cements, long predating GIC and resin cements.

mcqs.q: Which water-based cement is NOT zinc phosphate or ZOE?
mcqs.explain: Water-based cements include glass ionomer, zinc polycarboxylate and zinc phosphate; ZOE is oil-based.

mcqs.q: The antibacterial action of ZOE is mainly due to:
mcqs.explain: Eugenol gives ZOE its antibacterial and sedative properties.

mcqs.q: Why might zinc phosphate need a base placed beneath it in a deep cavity?
opts: Its low initial pH can irritate the pulp
mcqs.explain: The acidic (low-pH) freshly-mixed zinc phosphate can irritate a near-pulpal area, so a protective liner/base may be indicated.

saqs.q: Define a dental cement and list four uses.
saqs.a: A substance that hardens to act as a base, liner, filling or adhesive. Uses: liner/base, luting, pulp capping, root-canal sealing (also restoration, periodontal pack).

saqs.q: Classify cements by matrix (Craig) with an example of each.
Give the composition and setting product of ZOE.
saqs.a: Powder = zinc oxide; liquid = eugenol. Setting forms zinc eugenolate (chelate).

saqs.q: List the properties of ZOE and a key contraindication.
saqs.a: Obtundant/sedative, antibacterial, but weak/soluble. Do not use under composite (eugenol inhibits resin polymerization).

saqs.q: Give the composition of zinc phosphate cement.
saqs.a: Powder = zinc oxide + magnesium oxide; liquid = phosphoric acid + water.

saqs.q: Why is zinc phosphate mixed on a cool glass slab?
saqs.a: Its setting is exothermic; a cool slab dissipates heat, slows the reaction and allows more powder for strength.

saqs.q: Give the main property, drawback and use of zinc phosphate.
saqs.a: Property: high compressive strength. Drawback: initially acidic (pulp irritation). Use: luting crowns/bridges/bands.
